newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold ends barely weaker, platinum slumps.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold ends barely weaker, platinum slumps.

text.p: TOCOM yen-based gold futures ended barely weaker on Friday, reflecting a dip in bullion prices overnight, and platinum slumped on long liquidation ahead of Monday's expiry of the spot October contract, traders said.
TOCOM most-active August 1997 gold futures settled one yen lower at 1,377 yen per gram. Spot October was up two at 1,394 yen while the others went out flat to two lower.

Bullishness in the dollar late in the session helped gold futures partially offset the overnight weakness in bullion, although the August contract was unable to reach Thursday's eight-month high of 1,380.
Bullion ended at $382.80/10 an ounce, little changed from New York's closing quote of $382.85/25, but off Thursday's Tokyo close of $383.65/95.
One trade house source expected Australian producer selling to weigh on prices above $383, although Asian physical demand below $382.50 should help fuel a test of resistance at $385.

TOCOM benchmark August platinum settled six yen lower at 1,385 yen per gram, while the premium to August gold slid to a bare eight yen. Spot October, which expires on Monday, ended four yen lower at 1,403 yen and the other months were three to six yen lower.
